issues.legal_issue: A writ petition challenging a land acquisition may be refused where it is brought after inordinate and unexplained delay by landowners who knew of and participated in the acquisition proceedings.
material_facts: The landowners challenged the acquisition 16 years after the award was made.
They had been aware of the acquisition and had participated in proceedings before the Land Acquisition Collector.
They gave no explanation for the delay.
The High Court allowed the petition by relying on an earlier decision, without addressing the objection of delay and laches.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have entertained the writ petition; the appeal was allowed, the High Court’s judgment was set aside, and the writ petition was dismissed on the ground of delay and laches.
issues.legal_principle: Relief under Article 226 is discretionary, and a court may refuse it where a petitioner has delayed without satisfactory explanation and the circumstances make relief inappropriate. The same principle concerning stale claims was recognized under Article 32 in Rabindranath Bose v. Union of India and applies to Article 226, as confirmed in Yunus (Baboobhai) A. Hamid Padvekar v. State of Maharashtra. The Court also relied on Durga Prashad v. Chief Controller of Imports and Exports, including its reliance on Smt. Narayani Devi Khaitan v. State of Bihar; Tridip Kumar Dingal v. State of West Bengal; P.S. Sadasivaswamy v. State of Tamil Nadu; P. Chinnanna v. State of A.P.; Hari Singh v. State of U.P.; and Printers (Mysore) Ltd. v. M.A. Rasheed. In land-acquisition cases, courts should be particularly cautious about entertaining stale challenges because setting aside acquisitions may cause public loss and delay projects for the general good. The Court stated that the approach in Dayal Singh v. Union of India was not consonant with the Constitution Bench decision in Rabindranath Bose, which Dayal Singh had not noticed.

rule.if: land_acquisition_writ_challenge and petition_filed_after_inordinate_delay and delay_unexplained and petitioners_knew_of_acquisition and petitioners_participated_in_acquisition

predicates.land_acquisition_writ_challenge: The petitioners brought a writ proceeding challenging the acquisition of land.
predicates.petition_filed_after_inordinate_delay: The petitioners waited an inordinate length of time after the acquisition award before bringing the petition.
predicates.delay_unexplained: The petitioners gave no satisfactory explanation for the time they waited to bring the petition.
predicates.petitioners_knew_of_acquisition: The petitioners knew that their land was being acquired.
predicates.petitioners_participated_in_acquisition: The petitioners took part in proceedings before the land-acquisition authority.

issues.definition: When landowners bring a writ challenge to an acquisition after an inordinate and unexplained delay despite knowing of and participating in the acquisition proceedings, the court denies writ relief for delay.
